stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician trainee working under the direct supervision of a pharmacist is asked to answer the pharmacy telephone during a staffing crunch and take a new prescription from a prescriber's agent. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: The trainee may take the prescription while under direct supervision.
The trainee may take the prescription if the pharmacist listens on a second handset.
The trainee may take the prescription if it is for a Schedule VI drug.
The trainee may not take prescriptions over the telephone.
The trainee may take the prescription after 500 hours of trainee employment.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 8.03(4)(b) allows a pharmacy technician trainee to perform the duties of a pharmacy technician under direct pharmacist supervision, but 247 CMR 8.03(4)(c) carves out an express exception: a trainee may not take prescriptions over the telephone. Direct supervision does not lift that carve-out.

choice_analysis.A: Direct supervision is the general condition, but the telephone carve-out overrides it.
choice_analysis.B: Monitoring the call does not remove the express prohibition.
choice_analysis.C: The prohibition is not limited by schedule.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: trainees may not take prescriptions over the telephone.
choice_analysis.E: The 500-hour figure relates to technician licensure eligibility, not telephone authority.

related_facts: A pharmacy technician trainee must be at least 16 years of age, while a pharmacy technician must be at least 18.
explanation.mpje_trap: A general grant of technician duties does not survive an express carve-out written into the same section.

reasoning_steps: Start from the general rule that a trainee may perform technician duties under direct supervision
Locate the express telephone carve-out that applies to trainees only
Apply the carve-out despite the supervision being in place
